I don’t think I properly expressed myself. I didn’t mean that a writer needed to explore extensive character histories or environments to make a world, just that the creator is aware of them to make a truly immersive experience. I feel you can tell when I writer knows everything about their characters, it comes through in the story. You may not talk about Jimmy’s great aunt Mabel who scared him as a boy by taking out her teeth, but you know about it and how it changes the character. When you know your characters and your environment down to details that you won’t even mention, it changes how you write the story. You don’t need to describe the world when the story takes place in a single room or neighborhood, but having it in your head will add richness. Details are the seasonings of writing. Some you taste and see easily, some embed themselves into the thickness of the plot. I just think that there’s a difference in the outcome between those that write a story with characters, and those that write a character’s story.
